Here is what I found in the project (pass 1).

## Part 1

The code is split into a client, a shared core and a server. The client draws the threads; the core holds the connection and the timeline; the server runs the agents.

- The client keeps every open thread in memory and draws only what is visible.
- The core reads the server's events and turns them into rows.
- The server writes each event to its database before it sends it.

```rust
pub fn visible_rows(rows: &[Row], top: f32, height: f32) -> &[Row] {
    let first = rows.partition_point(|row| row.bottom() < top);
    let last = rows.partition_point(|row| row.top() < top + height);
    &rows[first..last]
}
```

| Part | Lines | Tests |
|---|---:|---:|
| client | 110,000 | 1,240 |
| core | 18,500 | 412 |
| server | 64,000 | 2,031 |
